# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **Six intercepted missiles bring French soldiers to guard Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil port.**

**What You Need to Know:** Six intercepted missiles bring French soldiers to guard Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil port. President Emmanuel Macron said France would send soldiers, radar and defence systems and would not join the fighting, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan prepare an urgent chiefs-of-staff meeting. Separate reporting covers two Israeli reservists killed in northern Gaza and an Iranian proposal on ending the war.

### Lead
**France to protect key Saudi oil terminal as Houthis step up missile attacks: South China Morning Post**

President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday that France will send soldiers, radar systems and defence systems to protect the Saudi oil port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, and that French forces will not take part in combat. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted missiles fired toward Yanbu and the city of Taif. Saudi authorities reported intercepting six ballistic missiles, while the Houthis said they launched dozens of missiles and drones on Thursday. The kingdom had issued emergency warnings for Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry said Friday that the kingdom, Turkey and Pakistan will hold an urgent meeting of their chiefs of staff on support for Riyadh. Under the Mecca Agreement, the ministry says an attack on one party is an attack on all. The three foreign ministers have already met, condemned attacks on Mecca and other civilian sites, and reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's right to self-defense. Saudi Arabia's Grand Mufti called on the military to be ready to give their lives until the Houthis are removed from power, the state news agency said late Thursday. Source: [scmp.com](https://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/3368772/france-protect-key-saudi-oil-terminal-houthis-step-missile-attacks)

### Across the Region
**Two reservists killed in northern Gaza as recovered IDF drone explodes: Haaretz**

Two Israeli reservists were killed in the northern Gaza Strip after an Israeli military drone crashed at an army outpost, Haaretz reports. Master Sgt. Nadav Kali, 24, from Jerusalem, and Master Sgt. Ofek Moalem, 23, picked the drone up. It then detonated. Source: [haaretz.com](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-09-25/ty-article/.premium/no-no-no/000001a0-d614-db4b-a7a5-d676b3c10000)

**Iran says it has given Trump administration new proposal for peace talks: The Washington Post**

Iran says it has given the Trump administration a new proposal for peace talks, The Washington Post reports, and The New York Times reports Iran has proposed a seven-day plan to end the war. The National reports that Iran has hardened its position on the Strait of Hormuz and insists Washington meet its conditions before formal negotiations resume. About 80 countries have backed a call for the urgent reopening of the waterway, and diplomacy at the UN General Assembly has yet to produce a breakthrough. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that it is America that must choose whether it wants to end the war. The United Arab Emirates has suspended all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice. Source: [washingtonpost.com](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/09/24/iran-says-it-has-given-trump-administration-new-proposal-peace-talks/)

### Also Today
**Ghana's aviation regulator supports entry of new carriers into domestic market: MyJoyOnline**

Ghana's Civil Aviation Authority says it is ready to admit new domestic airlines to strengthen competition and help reduce fares, and Director General Stephen Wilfred Arthur says the regulator does not set ticket prices. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/world/aviatsiinii-reguliator-gani-pidtrimav-vikhid-novikh-pereviznikiv-na-vnutrishnii-rinok-myjoyonline)

**Internet disruption seen in war-hit northern Ethiopia, web monitor says: Reuters**

A web monitor has seen an internet disruption in war-hit northern Ethiopia, Reuters reports. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/internet-disruption-seen-war-hit-northern-ethiopia-web-monitor-says-2026-09-25/)

**Kenya to double Ethiopian power imports as domestic grid pressures mount: The Africa Report**

Kenya is to double electricity imports from Ethiopia as pressure mounts on the domestic grid, The Africa Report reports. Source: [theafricareport.com](https://www.theafricareport.com/431601/kenya-to-double-ethiopian-power-imports-as-domestic-grid-pressures-mount/)

### The Region and the World
**Colombia formally cuts ties with Iran: Middle East Eye**

Colombia's foreign ministry said Thursday that the country has formally severed diplomatic relations with Iran, with the decision taking effect on Saturday. The ministry cited national and hemispheric security concerns. It accused Iran of human rights violations and alleged links to international terrorist and narcoterrorist groups. It also cited confirmed human rights violations, attacks on countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and obstruction of International Atomic Energy Agency efforts to verify Iran's nuclear programme. The ministry said those facts had deteriorated Colombia's trust in the government in Tehran. Source: [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/colombia-formally-cuts-ties-iran)

### Both Sides: Whether talks wait on Washington meeting Iran's conditions

The question is whether formal negotiations to end the war, and any reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, wait until Washington meets Iran's conditions.

Iran's case, as its president states it, is that the choice sits in Washington. Masoud Pezeshkian told Fox News that America must choose whether it wants to end the war, after he was asked if it could end by the end of the year. The National reports that Tehran has hardened its position on the strait and insists Washington meet its conditions before formal negotiations resume. The Washington Post reports that Iran says it has given the Trump administration a new proposal for peace talks, and The New York Times reports that Iran has proposed a seven-day plan to end the war. The strongest reason on this side is sequence: Iranian officials are putting a proposal forward and describing an end to the fighting as America's decision, with conditions before formal talks.

The case for not waiting on that sequence comes from governments treating the closure as the emergency. The National reports that about 80 countries have backed a call for the urgent reopening of the waterway, and that diplomacy at the UN General Assembly has yet to produce a breakthrough. The United Arab Emirates has suspended all flights operated by Iranian airlines to and from the country until further notice. Colombia's foreign ministry, in cutting ties, cited the blockade of the strait, obstruction of International Atomic Energy Agency checks, attacks on countries not involved in the conflict, and human rights violations. The strongest reason on this side is that a wide group of states is asking for the waterway to reopen now, while some governments are already cutting flights and relations over the blockade and the war.

Iran's stated conditions and the eighty-country call both treat the strait as not open in the ordinary way, and both sit against talks that The National says have not broken through. The proposal is now with the Trump administration, and the Emirati suspension runs until further notice.

### Progress Watch
**Daily Maverick opens the DM168 e-edition to every registered reader for World News Day: Daily Maverick**

Daily Maverick is making the DM168 e-edition free to every registered user from Friday, 25 September 2026, for World News Day on Monday, 28 September, which is also the United Nations International Day for Universal Access to Information. Anyone who signs up with an email address can read the full weekly digital edition at no cost. South Africans vote in local government elections on 4 November. More than 1,000 newsrooms in more than 100 countries are marking the day. Co-founder Branko Brkic wrote that the right to know is real only if someone makes information easy to find, check and true. Source: [dailymaverick.co.za](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-25-daily-maverick-opens-the-dm168-e-edition-to-every-registered-reader-for-world-news-day/)

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **South Africa's central bank raised its repo rate by a quarter point to seven point two five percent, pushing up loan costs for borrowers.**
The unanimous decision by the Monetary Policy Committee responds to inflation projected to peak at five point seven percent in November and a zero point two percent GDP contraction in the second quarter. Headline inflation stood at four point four percent in August while services inflation reached five point one percent.

### Lead
**Economic fire — Interest rate adjustment makes for interesting braai chat: Daily Maverick**
The Monetary Policy Committee of the South African Reserve Bank voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by twenty five basis points from seven percent to seven point two five percent. The prime lending rate rose automatically from ten point five percent to ten point seven five percent. Headline inflation reached four point four percent in August while the central bank projects it will peak at five point seven percent in November. Services inflation stood at five point one percent in August. The economy contracted zero point two percent in the second quarter of twenty twenty six, prompting the bank to lower its full year GDP growth forecast to one point two percent. Market analysts viewed the move as a preventive step to anchor expectations rather than the start of a longer tightening cycle. Chief Economist Johann Els at PSG Financial Services noted the unanimous vote was more hawkish than expected. Supply side price shocks are initially inflationary but ultimately deflationary for demand and growth according to Els. The adjustment marks the second such increase since the government ended austerity measures. The decision came the day before Heritage Day when many South Africans gather for braais. Archbishop Desmond Tutu had earlier linked the day to braai celebrations which boosted retail sales. The bank cited elevated long term inflation expectations above its three percent midpoint target as a key factor. Source: [dailymaverick.co.za](https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2026-09-24-economic-fire-interest-rate-adjustment-makes-for-interesting-braai-chat/)

### Across the Region
**CAR Rebel Commander Convicted of Crimes Against Humanity: AllAfrica**
The International Criminal Court convicted Central African Republic Seleka rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani on four counts including torture and persecution for acts during the twenty thirteen conflict. Prosecutors said Said ran a Bangui prison where suspected supporters of former president François Bozizé were beaten and held in a windowless cell beneath his office floorboards. Central African Republic Justice Minister Arnaud Djoubaye Abazène welcomed the ruling and said no victim will be left behind. The twenty thirteen seizure of power by predominantly Muslim Seleka rebels triggered opposition from mainly Christian anti Balaka militias. Detainees testified about beatings and harsh conditions in the prison. The conviction covers events from the height of the conflict that ousted President Bozizé. Source: [allafrica.com](https://allafrica.com/stories/202609240254.html)

**Drone strikes kill 10 at Sudan court and college: Business Day**
Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces carried out drone attacks on government held towns in North Kordofan state. One strike hit a crowded courtroom in Um Ruwaba on September eight and killed about ten people while injuring dozens according to Emergency Lawyers. A second strike the next day hit a college in al Obeid killing a security guard and damaging eight classrooms. The dean of the college said the entire faculty felt destroyed. A student who had taken exams the previous day described her future as destroyed. The United Nations reported that drone attacks by both sides killed more than one thousand civilians in the first half of the year. Residents described the strikes as part of a new campaign after weeks of reduced activity. The Rapid Support Forces said it does not intentionally target civilians. A hospital patient in Um Ruwaba who fled earlier bombardment distinguished between strategic and suicide drones. Source: [businessday.co.za](https://www.businessday.co.za/world/africa/2026-09-24-drone-strikes-kill-10-at-sudan-court-and-college/)

### Also Today
**'GMA is monitoring Ghana's marine space blindly’ – Miracles Aboagye: modernghana.com**
New Patriotic Party communicator Dennis Miracles Aboagye said Ghana's Vessel Traffic Management Information System has been out of operation at sites including Ada Winneba Axim Keta and Half Assini forcing reliance on a less comprehensive Skylight system. The communicator argued that the system cannot provide continuous coverage for detecting smaller vessels outside port limits. He linked the surveillance gap to increased risks of narcotics movement through Ghana's maritime domain. The Ghana Maritime Authority rejected the claim and said its systems remain operational. Aboagye maintained that the collapse of the Vessel Traffic Management Information System removed a key detection and interception layer. Source: [modernghana.com](https://www.modernghana.com/news/1530390/gma-is-monitoring-ghanas-marine-space-blindly.html)

**US Mineral Investment Could Accelerate Nigeria’s Industrial and Logistics Development: nigeriahousingmarket.com**
Nigeria and the United States signed a framework agreement for cooperation in geological data mineral development processing and infrastructure with Nigeria's Minister of Solid Minerals Development Dele Alake stating the goal is to retain more value inside the country through local processing. The agreement was signed in New York by Alake and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau. It covers the mineral value chain from exploration through development and processing. Alake said Nigeria does not want to remain primarily an exporter of raw minerals. The pact identifies infrastructure as one area for cooperation that could stimulate demand for industrial property and logistics facilities near production areas. Source: [nigeriahousingmarket.com](https://www.nigeriahousingmarket.com/news/nigeria-us-mining-pact-industrial-logistics-property)

### The Region and the World
**Djibouti, Ethiopia and Dangote plan petroleum pipeline, Ethiopian PM says: Reuters**
Djibouti Ethiopia and the Dangote group plan a petroleum pipeline that would link Ethiopian refineries to the port of Djibouti according to Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. The project aims to improve export routes for refined petroleum products. It would connect inland production sites to coastal facilities in Djibouti. The announcement came during regional economic discussions. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/djibouti-ethiopia-dangote-plan-petroleum-pipeline-ethiopian-pm-says-2026-09-24/)

### Both Sides: Ghana maritime surveillance effectiveness
Ghana's opposition and the Ghana Maritime Authority disagree on whether the Vessel Traffic Management Information System remains fully operational for monitoring the country's waters. Miracles Aboagye of the New Patriotic Party argues the system has been down for months at multiple coastal sites and that reliance on the Skylight alternative leaves smaller vessels and activities outside port limits undetected increasing risks of narcotics movement. The Ghana Maritime Authority states its systems remain operational for monitoring activities within Ghana’s maritime space. Both sides accept that continuous detection capability matters for intercepting illicit consignments. The next step is continued public statements from both the authority and opposition figures without a scheduled resolution date. Aboagye specifically named sites at Ada Winneba Axim Keta and Half Assini as affected. He said the CCTV cameras at those sites were also not functioning. The authority issued a statement on September twenty three rejecting the claims of downtime.

# Omni View Africa & Middle East
> **At least 11 people were killed in a mass shooting near Durban.**

**What You Need to Know:** Gunmen killed at least 11 people in a house in KwaMakhutha, near Durban, late on Tuesday. The UK is reviewing its deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius after President Donald Trump called that deal terrible. Syria’s president, at the UN General Assembly, condemned Israeli attacks and described a year of change at home.

### What This Show Covers
You want one region, every day, told straight: what was decided, what happened, what it changes and for whom. One contested question is set out with the strongest case on each side, and the day is checked for one measurable sign of progress. That is the job — not a tour of every capital, and not a verdict.

This desk covers the African continent, the Arabian Peninsula and the Gulf, the Levant, Iran and Iraq. A story filed somewhere else is here only for a concrete consequence inside that region, and that consequence is stated first.

The brief is read by Mira, the network’s AI host. The stories are chosen and written by software from named newsrooms, and every item names its source. The one thing it will not do is take a side — every claim is attributed, and no party, government or people is praised or mocked.

The other Omni View desks and Omni View Top World News sit alongside this one.

Omni View Africa & Middle East is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com. Listen if it is useful; nothing is being sold with the invitation.

### Lead
**11 killed in mass shooting near Durban, South Africa: BBC News Africa**
Gunmen stormed a house in the KwaMakhutha township, near the South African city of Durban, late on Tuesday and opened fire on 14 people. At least 11 people were killed in that residential building. For the people inside that house, the attack is the day’s hardest counted loss. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crgjqxzl097eo)

### Across the Region
**South African police officer charged with sexual offences: BBC News Africa**
Lieutenant General Shadrack Sibiya, one of South Africa’s highest-ranking police officers, has been charged with sexual offences. He made a brief appearance at a court north-west of Johannesburg. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwjdvgx77n0zo)

**Al-Sharaa condemns Israel’s attacks on Syria, calls for 1974 agreement commitment: Al Jazeera English**
Syria’s President Ahmed al-Sharaa opened his UN General Assembly speech by praising what he called Syria’s “breakthrough” over the past year. He said the country had transformed “from a crisis to an opportunity” under his leadership, which is his account of the year, not an independent finding. He condemned Israel’s attacks on Syria and called for a commitment to the 1974 agreement. Source: [aljazeera.com](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/23/un-general-assembly-live-irans-pezeshkian-ukraines-zelenskyy-to-speak)

**French FM Calls for Palestinians to Hold Polls: Arab News**
France’s foreign minister has called for Palestinians to hold polls. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/arabnews/status/2102758481325359126)

### The Region and the World
**UK reviewing Chagos Islands deal after Trump criticism: BBC News Africa**
Mauritius’s agreed handover of the Chagos Islands is no longer being treated in London as settled. The UK is reviewing its deal to hand the islands to Mauritius. Defence secretary Wes Streeting confirmed the deal was being looked at after US President Donald Trump called it “terrible” at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. Source: [bbc.com](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck3wjy3pdwdno)

### Both Sides: The Chagos transfer
What is being decided is whether the UK goes ahead with its deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. Defence secretary Wes Streeting has confirmed the deal is being looked at. BBC News Africa reported that the review follows US President Donald Trump, who at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday called the deal “terrible”.

The case against letting the transfer stand, as Trump made it, is that judgment. He called the deal terrible before the General Assembly. Streeting’s confirmation that the deal is being reviewed comes after that criticism. The reason Trump gave, in the words the report carries, is that the deal is terrible.

The arrangement that criticism is aimed at is the UK deal to hand the Chagos Islands to Mauritius. Streeting’s stated position is that this deal is being looked at. That review is the British official position on the record today: not a fresh defence of the transfer, and not a statement that the handover has been replaced by another plan.

The fact the criticism and the review share is that a deal exists to hand the islands to Mauritius, that the defence secretary says it is being looked at, and that Trump called it terrible at the General Assembly on Tuesday. The next step the report names is that review.

### Progress Watch
**150 Women Graduate from Syria's New Police Academy: Arab News**
Some 150 women have graduated from Syria’s new police academy in Al-Tal, north of Damascus. That is a completed first cohort, not a pledge of future recruitment. Source: [arabnews.com](https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/first-cohort-of-syrian-policewomen-graduate-from-new-academy-3002728)
